tools.keyword-density.faqs.0.question: What is keyword density?
tools.keyword-density.faqs.0.answer: Keyword density is the percentage of times a keyword or phrase appears in your content compared to the total number of words. It is calculated as (keyword occurrences ÷ total words) × 100.
tools.keyword-density.faqs.1.question: What is a good keyword density?
tools.keyword-density.faqs.1.answer: A keyword density between 1% and 3% is generally considered optimal for SEO. Going much higher can look like keyword stuffing, which search engines may penalize.
tools.keyword-density.faqs.2.question: How is the density calculated in this tool?
tools.keyword-density.faqs.2.answer: The tool counts every word in your content, then divides the occurrences of each keyword by the total word count and multiplies by 100. You can set a minimum word length to ignore very short words.
tools.keyword-density.faqs.3.question: Why should I check keyword density?
tools.keyword-density.faqs.3.answer: Checking keyword density helps you confirm your primary keywords appear frequently enough for search engines to understand your topic, without overusing them. It also helps you spot underused secondary keywords.
tools.keyword-density.faqs.4.question: Is my content sent to a server?
tools.keyword-density.faqs.4.answer: No. All analysis happens locally in your browser. Your content never leaves your device.
tools.keyword-density.guide.intro.title: What is a Keyword Density Checker?
tools.keyword-density.guide.intro.paragr: A keyword density checker is a free online tool that analyzes how often specific words or phrases appear in your content. It shows each keyword's count, frequency, and percentage of the total text so you can optimize your writing for search engines without keyword stuffing.
tools.keyword-density.guide.sections.0.p: Paste or type your content into the text area, set a minimum word length to filter out short filler words, choose how many top keywords to show, and click Analyze.
tools.keyword-density.guide.sections.0.i: Review the total and unique word counts for an overview of your content size.
Check each keyword's count and density percentage in the results table.
Aim for a density of 1% to 3% for your main keywords.
tools.keyword-density.guide.sections.1.p: Use your primary keyword in the title, headings, and first paragraph, then repeat it naturally throughout the body. Use this tool to verify you are not overusing it.
tools.keyword-density.guide.sections.1.i: Target a density of 1% to 3% for primary keywords.
Use related synonyms and long-tail variants for secondary keywords.
Keep the writing natural for readers first, search engines second.

tools.meta-tags-analyzer.faqs.0.question: What is a meta tags analyzer?
tools.meta-tags-analyzer.faqs.0.answer: A meta tags analyzer reads the title, meta description, keywords, Open Graph, Twitter Card, and other tags of a web page. It shows you what search engines and social networks see, and warns about missing or malformed tags.
tools.meta-tags-analyzer.faqs.1.question: Which meta tags does it check?
tools.meta-tags-analyzer.faqs.1.answer: It checks the title, meta description, keywords, robots, canonical link, H1, and social tags including Open Graph (og:title, og:description, og:image) and Twitter Cards.
tools.meta-tags-analyzer.faqs.2.question: Why can't it fetch some URLs?
tools.meta-tags-analyzer.faqs.2.answer: Browsers block cross-origin requests, so the page is fetched through a public proxy. Some sites block proxy requests or require JavaScript, which prevents fetching. In that case, use the Paste HTML mode.
tools.meta-tags-analyzer.faqs.3.question: Is my data stored?
tools.meta-tags-analyzer.faqs.3.answer: No. The page content is fetched and analyzed in your browser session only. Nothing is uploaded to our servers.
tools.meta-tags-analyzer.faqs.4.question: What makes good meta tags?
tools.meta-tags-analyzer.faqs.4.answer: A title under 60 characters, a meta description under 160 characters, an accurate H1, a canonical URL, and Open Graph and Twitter Card tags for social sharing. The analyzer warns you when these are missing or too long.
tools.meta-tags-analyzer.guide.intro.tit: What is a Meta Tags Analyzer?
tools.meta-tags-analyzer.guide.intro.par: A meta tags analyzer is a free online tool that fetches a web page and extracts all of its meta tags. It helps you audit how your page appears in search engine results and social media previews, and flags issues that can hurt your click-through rate.
Enter a page URL and click Analyze Meta Tags. The tool fetches the page through a proxy and lists every meta tag it finds.
Check that the title is under 60 characters.
Check that the meta description is under 160 characters.
Make sure Open Graph and Twitter Card tags are present for social sharing.
If a URL cannot be fetched, copy the page's HTML source and switch to the Paste HTML mode. This works for any page, including private or dynamic ones.
tools.long-tail-keywords.metadata.title: Long Tail Keyword Tool
tools.long-tail-keywords.metadata.descri: Generate long-tail keyword suggestions for your topic
tools.long-tail-keywords.faqs.0.question: What are long-tail keywords?
tools.long-tail-keywords.faqs.0.answer: Long-tail keywords are longer, more specific search phrases, such as 'best budget coffee maker for camping' instead of 'coffee maker'. They usually have lower search volume but much higher conversion intent.
tools.long-tail-keywords.faqs.1.question: How does this tool generate keywords?
tools.long-tail-keywords.faqs.1.answer: It combines your seed keyword with prefixes and suffixes such as 'best', 'how to', 'reviews', and location words, then generates combinations like 'how to use a french press' or 'best espresso machine reviews'.
tools.long-tail-keywords.faqs.2.question: Why are long-tail keywords important for SEO?
tools.long-tail-keywords.faqs.2.answer: They face less competition, are easier to rank for, and attract visitors who are closer to making a purchase or finding a specific answer.
tools.long-tail-keywords.faqs.3.question: How many keywords can I generate?
tools.long-tail-keywords.faqs.3.answer: The tool generates up to 60 suggestions per seed keyword, including country-specific and question-based variants. You can copy individual keywords or the whole list.
tools.long-tail-keywords.guide.intro.tit: What is a Long Tail Keyword Tool?
tools.long-tail-keywords.guide.intro.par: A long-tail keyword tool is a free generator that turns one seed keyword into dozens of longer, specific search phrases. It is a fast way to build keyword lists for blog posts, product pages, and SEO campaigns.
Enter a seed keyword, pick a target country or language, choose a category such as How To or Best / Top, and click Generate.
Use question keywords ('what is', 'how to') for informational content.
Use 'best', 'reviews', and 'buy' keywords for commercial pages.
Use 'near me' and country variants for local SEO.
Start with a broad seed keyword and let the tool expand it. Then filter the list to the phrases that match your audience's intent.

tools.keyword-position.faqs.0.question: How does the keyword position checker work?
tools.keyword-position.faqs.0.answer: For each keyword, the tool fetches the search engine results page through a proxy, parses the organic results, and finds the position where your domain appears.
tools.keyword-position.faqs.1.question: Which search engine does it check?
tools.keyword-position.faqs.1.answer: It checks Bing organic results. Browsers block direct requests to Google, so Bing is used as a reliable, accessible estimate of your ranking position.
tools.keyword-position.faqs.2.question: Why do positions differ between search engines?
tools.keyword-position.faqs.2.answer: Google and Bing use different ranking algorithms and indexes, so the same keyword can rank differently. The tool marks results as estimates for this reason.
tools.keyword-position.faqs.3.question: How many keywords can I check at once?
tools.keyword-position.faqs.3.answer: You can check any number of keywords, one per line. Larger lists take longer because each keyword requires a separate search request.
tools.keyword-position.guide.intro.title: What is a Keyword Position Checker?
tools.keyword-position.guide.intro.parag: A keyword position checker (or rank checker) shows where your website appears in search engine results for specific keywords. It helps you monitor your SEO progress without paying for expensive rank tracking software.
Enter your website URL and a list of keywords (one per line), then click Check Keyword Positions. The tool shows the position of each keyword and the matching result URL.
Positions 1 to 10 are the most valuable for organic traffic.
Keywords not found in the top 50 are shown as 'Not in top 50'.
Run the check regularly to track ranking changes over time.
Check keywords that already bring you traffic to understand your baseline, then focus on keywords in positions 11 to 30, which are easiest to push into the top 10.

tools.json-formatter.faqs.0.question: How do I format JSON online?
tools.json-formatter.faqs.0.answer: Paste your raw or minified JSON into the input field and click Format. The tool parses and pretty-prints it with your chosen indentation (2 spaces, 4 spaces, or tabs) and applies syntax highlighting for easy reading.
tools.json-formatter.faqs.1.question: How do I validate if my JSON is correct?
tools.json-formatter.faqs.1.answer: Click the Validate button after pasting your JSON. The tool will tell you whether the JSON is valid or display the exact parsing error with a description of what went wrong and where.
tools.json-formatter.faqs.2.question: What is the difference between formatting and minifying JSON?
tools.json-formatter.faqs.2.answer: Formatting adds whitespace and line breaks to make JSON human-readable. Minifying removes all unnecessary whitespace to produce the smallest possible output, which is useful for reducing payload size in APIs and config files.
tools.json-formatter.faqs.3.question: Can I format large JSON files in this tool?
tools.json-formatter.faqs.3.answer: Yes. Since the tool runs entirely in your browser, it can handle large JSON payloads. For files over 10 MB, you may experience a brief delay while parsing. There is no server-side limit.
tools.json-formatter.faqs.4.question: Is my JSON data sent to a server?
tools.json-formatter.faqs.4.answer: No. All formatting, minifying, and validation happens locally in your browser. Your data never leaves your device, making this tool safe for sensitive API responses and configuration files.
tools.json-formatter.faqs.5.question: Does the formatter support JSON with comments?
tools.json-formatter.faqs.5.answer: No. The tool uses the standard JSON parser which does not allow comments. If your JSON contains comments (JSONC), you will need to remove them before pasting. Consider using a JSONC-aware editor for commented files.

tools.base64-encoder.faqs.0.question: What is Base64 encoding?
tools.base64-encoder.faqs.0.answer: Base64 encoding converts binary data into a text format using 64 ASCII characters. It is commonly used to embed images in HTML or CSS, transmit binary data over text-based protocols like email, and store data in JSON or XML.
tools.base64-encoder.faqs.1.question: How do I encode text to Base64?
tools.base64-encoder.faqs.1.answer: Select the Encode mode, type or paste your text into the input field, and the Base64-encoded output appears instantly. Click the copy button to grab the result for use in your project.
tools.base64-encoder.faqs.2.question: How do I decode a Base64 string?
tools.base64-encoder.faqs.2.answer: Switch to Decode mode and paste your Base64 string into the input field. The tool automatically converts it back to readable text. If the string is invalid Base64, an error message is displayed.
tools.base64-encoder.faqs.3.question: Can I convert an image to Base64?
tools.base64-encoder.faqs.3.answer: Yes. Drag and drop an image file onto the upload area, or click to select a file. The tool generates a data URL with the Base64-encoded image, and shows a preview if it is an image file.
tools.base64-encoder.faqs.4.question: Does Base64 encoding encrypt my data?
tools.base64-encoder.faqs.4.answer: No. Base64 is an encoding scheme, not encryption. Anyone can decode a Base64 string to view the original data. Do not use Base64 as a security measure for sensitive information.
tools.base64-encoder.faqs.5.question: Why is my Base64 output larger than the original?
tools.base64-encoder.faqs.5.answer: Base64 encoding increases data size by approximately 33%. Every three bytes of input become four characters of Base64 output. This overhead is the tradeoff for safe text-based transmission of binary data.

tools.base64-to-image.faqs.0.answer: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, and SVG. The tool detects the format automatically from the Base64 header, so you do not need to specify it.
tools.base64-to-image.faqs.1.question: Do I need to include the data:image prefix?
tools.base64-to-image.faqs.1.answer: No. The tool accepts both raw Base64 strings and full data URLs that start with data:image/.... If the prefix is present, it is used to identify the format.
tools.base64-to-image.faqs.2.question: Is my data uploaded anywhere?
tools.base64-to-image.faqs.2.answer: No. All decoding happens locally in your browser. Your Base64 data never leaves your device.
tools.base64-to-image.faqs.3.question: Why does the tool say my string is not an image?
tools.base64-to-image.faqs.3.answer: The string may not be valid Base64, or it may encode something other than an image, such as text or a document. Double-check that you copied the full string.
tools.base64-to-image.faqs.4.question: How do I download the converted image?

tools.lorem-ipsum-generator.metadata.des: Generate placeholder text in paragraphs, sentences, or words.
tools.lorem-ipsum-generator.faqs.0.answe: Lorem Ipsum is placeholder text derived from a 1st-century BC Latin work by Cicero. Designers and developers use it to fill layouts before real content is available, allowing them to evaluate visual design without being distracted by readable text.
tools.lorem-ipsum-generator.faqs.1.quest: How do I generate Lorem Ipsum text?
tools.lorem-ipsum-generator.faqs.1.answe: Choose a type (paragraphs, sentences, or words), set the quantity you need, and click Generate. The placeholder text is created instantly and can be copied to your clipboard with one click.
tools.lorem-ipsum-generator.faqs.2.quest: Can I generate a specific number of paragraphs?
tools.lorem-ipsum-generator.faqs.2.answe: Yes. Set the type to Paragraphs and enter the number you need, from 1 to 100. Each generated paragraph contains a randomized mix of 3 to 7 Latin-style sentences.
tools.lorem-ipsum-generator.faqs.3.quest: What does the 'Start with Lorem ipsum' option do?
tools.lorem-ipsum-generator.faqs.3.answe: When enabled, the generated text begins with the traditional 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit' opening. Disable it if you want fully randomized placeholder text from the start.
tools.lorem-ipsum-generator.faqs.4.quest: Is Lorem Ipsum good for SEO testing?
tools.lorem-ipsum-generator.faqs.4.answe: Lorem Ipsum is useful for testing page layouts and typography but should never appear on a production site. Search engines may flag pages with Latin placeholder text as low-quality or incomplete content.
tools.lorem-ipsum-generator.faqs.5.quest: Can I use this generated text commercially?
tools.lorem-ipsum-generator.faqs.5.answe: Yes. Lorem Ipsum text is not copyrighted and can be used freely in mockups, wireframes, prototypes, and design presentations. It is intended solely as placeholder content and should be replaced before launch.

tools.uuid-generator.faqs.0.question: What is a UUID?
tools.uuid-generator.faqs.0.answer: A UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) is a 128-bit identifier formatted as a 32-character hexadecimal string with hyphens. UUID v4, which this tool generates, uses random values, making collisions virtually impossible across systems without coordination.
tools.uuid-generator.faqs.1.question: What is the difference between UUID and GUID?
tools.uuid-generator.faqs.1.answer: UUID and GUID (Globally Unique Identifier) are the same concept. UUID is the standard term used by the IETF and in most programming languages, while GUID is the term commonly used in Microsoft technologies. The format and purpose are identical.
tools.uuid-generator.faqs.2.question: Can I generate multiple UUIDs at once?
tools.uuid-generator.faqs.2.answer: Yes. Enter the quantity you need (up to 100) and click Bulk Generate. All UUIDs appear in a scrollable list. You can copy individual UUIDs or click Copy All to grab the entire list at once.
tools.uuid-generator.faqs.3.question: Are generated UUIDs truly unique?
tools.uuid-generator.faqs.3.answer: UUID v4 uses cryptographically random values, providing 122 bits of randomness. The probability of generating a duplicate is astronomically low, effectively making each UUID unique for all practical purposes.
tools.uuid-generator.faqs.4.question: Can I remove hyphens from generated UUIDs?
tools.uuid-generator.faqs.4.answer: Yes. Uncheck the Hyphens option to generate UUIDs without dashes. This produces a continuous 32-character hexadecimal string, which some systems and databases prefer.
tools.uuid-generator.faqs.5.question: When should I use UUIDs instead of auto-increment IDs?
tools.uuid-generator.faqs.5.answer: Use UUIDs when you need identifiers that are unique across distributed systems without a central authority. They are ideal for microservices, client-side ID generation, database merging, and scenarios where sequential IDs would reveal record counts.

tools.uuid-generator.guide.sections.3.pa: UUID version 4 generates identifiers using random or pseudo-random numbers. Of the 128 bits, 122 are random and 6 are fixed to indicate the version and variant. This produces over 5.3 undecillion possible combinations, making the chance of a collision negligibly small even at massive scale.
All generation happens client-side in your browser. No UUIDs are sent to or stored on any server, so you can safely generate identifiers for any project without privacy concerns.

tools.word-counter.faqs.0.question: How do I count words in my text?
tools.word-counter.faqs.0.answer: Paste or type your text into the input area. The word count updates instantly in the statistics panel on the right. The tool also shows character count, sentence count, paragraph count, and estimated reading time.
tools.word-counter.faqs.1.question: Does the word counter include spaces in the character count?
tools.word-counter.faqs.1.answer: The tool provides both counts. The Characters stat includes spaces, while the Characters (no spaces) stat excludes them. This is useful for platforms that count characters differently.
tools.word-counter.faqs.2.question: How is reading time calculated?
tools.word-counter.faqs.2.answer: Reading time is estimated at an average rate of 200 words per minute, which is the standard for adult reading speed. The result is rounded up to the nearest minute to give a practical estimate.
tools.word-counter.faqs.3.question: What does the word frequency feature show?
tools.word-counter.faqs.3.answer: The Top Words section displays the 10 most frequently used words in your text along with their occurrence count and a visual bar chart. Single-letter words are excluded to focus on meaningful terms.
tools.word-counter.faqs.4.question: Can I use this to check essay word limits?
tools.word-counter.faqs.4.answer: Yes. Paste your essay or assignment text and instantly see the word count, character count, and paragraph count. This helps you stay within submission requirements for school, college, or professional writing.
tools.word-counter.faqs.5.question: Does this tool work for languages other than English?
tools.word-counter.faqs.5.answer: The word counter works with any language that separates words with spaces. It counts words by splitting on whitespace. Character counting works for all languages and Unicode text.

tools.word-counter.guide.intro.title: What Is the Word Counter?
tools.word-counter.guide.intro.paragraph: The Word Counter is an online text analysis tool that instantly counts words, characters, sentences, and paragraphs in any text you enter. It also estimates reading time and reveals your most frequently used words. Whether you are writing an essay, blog post, or social media caption, this tool helps you hit your targets.
tools.word-counter.guide.sections.0.titl: How to Use the Word Counter
tools.word-counter.guide.sections.0.para: Using the tool is straightforward. Paste or type your text and all statistics update in real time.
tools.word-counter.guide.sections.0.item: Paste your text into the large input area, or start typing directly.
View word count, character count, and more in the Statistics panel.
Check the Characters (no spaces) stat for platforms with strict character limits.
See the estimated reading time based on 200 words per minute.
Review the Top Words section to identify overused terms.
Use the copy button to copy your text after reviewing the stats.
tools.word-counter.guide.sections.1.para: The tool provides five core metrics: word count, total characters, characters without spaces, sentence count, and paragraph count. Sentences are detected by periods, exclamation marks, and question marks. Paragraphs are split by blank lines.

Reading time is calculated at 200 words per minute, which is a widely accepted average for adult reading speed. The word frequency chart highlights your top 10 most-used words, helping you spot repetition in your writing.
tools.word-counter.guide.sections.2.item: Meeting word count requirements for essays, articles, and assignments.
Checking character limits for tweets, meta descriptions, and SMS.
Estimating reading time for blog posts and newsletters.
Identifying overused words to improve writing quality.
Verifying paragraph and sentence counts for structured writing.
tools.word-counter.guide.sections.3.para: Use the word frequency analysis to spot words you repeat too often. If a non-essential word appears at the top of the list, consider replacing some instances with synonyms or restructuring your sentences. Aim for variety to keep your writing engaging and clear.
tools.word-counter.description: Count words, characters, sentences, and paragraphs. Analyze reading time and word frequency.

tools.image-color-picker.faqs.0.question: How do I pick a color from an image online?
tools.image-color-picker.faqs.0.answer: Upload your image to this tool by dragging it onto the page or clicking the upload area. Once loaded, click anywhere on the image and the tool instantly shows you the HEX, RGB, and HSL color values for that pixel.
tools.image-color-picker.faqs.1.question: What image formats does the color picker support?
tools.image-color-picker.faqs.1.answer: The tool supports all common web image formats including PNG, JPG/JPEG, GIF, and WebP. Any image your browser can display can be used with this color picker.
tools.image-color-picker.faqs.2.question: Can I pick multiple colors from the same image?
tools.image-color-picker.faqs.2.answer: Yes. Every color you click is added to the Recent Picks palette, which stores up to 10 colors. You can click any swatch in the palette to revisit its color values and copy them.
tools.image-color-picker.faqs.3.question: Is the image color picker accurate for design work?
tools.image-color-picker.faqs.3.answer: The tool samples exact pixel values from the loaded image, so it is pixel-accurate. For best results with design work, use high-resolution PNG or lossless images, since JPEG compression can alter colors slightly.
tools.image-color-picker.faqs.4.question: Does this tool upload my images to a server?
tools.image-color-picker.faqs.4.answer: No. Everything runs entirely in your browser. Your images are processed locally using the HTML5 Canvas API and are never uploaded to any server.
tools.image-color-picker.faqs.5.question: How do I convert HEX color to RGB from an image?
tools.image-color-picker.faqs.5.answer: Simply upload your image and click on the color you want. The tool automatically displays the color in all three formats at once: HEX, RGB, and HSL. You can copy whichever format you need.
tools.image-color-picker.guide.intro.tit: What Is the Image Color Picker?
tools.image-color-picker.guide.intro.par: The Image Color Picker lets you extract exact colors from any image right in your browser. Upload a photo, screenshot, or design file, then click anywhere on the image to instantly get the color value in HEX, RGB, and HSL formats. No software installation required.

Whether you are matching brand colors from a logo, sampling colors from a photograph for a design project, or identifying the exact shade used on a website screenshot, this tool gives you pixel-perfect accuracy in one click.
How to Use the Image Color Picker
Drag and drop an image onto the upload area, or click to select a file from your device. PNG, JPG, GIF, and WebP formats are supported.
Once the image loads, hover over it and click on any pixel. The crosshair cursor guides your selection.
The picked color appears in the sidebar with its HEX, RGB, and HSL values. Click the copy button next to any format to copy it to your clipboard.
Every color you pick is saved to the Recent Picks palette. Click any swatch to revisit a previously sampled color.
Use the Change Image button to load a different file without refreshing the page.

For the best results, use high-resolution images. Compressed JPEGs may introduce color artifacts around edges. If you need a color from a specific area, zoom into your image in an editor first and then take a screenshot of the zoomed region before uploading.

The tool scales large images to fit the canvas while preserving aspect ratio. The color values are sampled from the scaled image pixels, so results are consistent regardless of the original file size.
Extracting brand colors from a client logo or marketing material
Matching paint or fabric colors from a reference photo
Sampling color palettes from photography or artwork for design inspiration
Identifying HEX codes from website screenshots for CSS development
Building a color palette from a mood board image

Every picked color is displayed in three standard formats. HEX codes like #3b82f6 are commonly used in CSS and web design. RGB values are useful for graphic design software and digital displays. HSL values provide an intuitive way to understand a color in terms of hue, saturation, and lightness, making adjustments easier.
tools.aspect-ratio-calculator.metadata.d: Calculate and visualize aspect ratios with presets
tools.aspect-ratio-calculator.faqs.0.que: How do I calculate the aspect ratio of an image?
tools.aspect-ratio-calculator.faqs.0.ans: Enter the image width and height in pixels into the calculator. It automatically simplifies the ratio using the greatest common divisor. For example, a 1920x1080 image returns 16:9.
tools.aspect-ratio-calculator.faqs.1.que: What is the aspect ratio of 1920x1080?
tools.aspect-ratio-calculator.faqs.1.ans: 1920x1080 has an aspect ratio of 16:9. This is the standard Full HD widescreen ratio used by most monitors, TVs, and video streaming platforms.
tools.aspect-ratio-calculator.faqs.2.que: How do I resize an image without distortion?
tools.aspect-ratio-calculator.faqs.2.ans: Enter your current dimensions, then click the lock button to lock the ratio. Now when you change either the width or height, the other dimension adjusts automatically to maintain the exact proportion, preventing any stretching or distortion.
tools.aspect-ratio-calculator.faqs.3.que: What aspect ratio should I use for YouTube videos?
tools.aspect-ratio-calculator.faqs.3.ans: YouTube recommends 16:9 for standard videos. Use the 16:9 preset in this calculator to find the right dimensions. For YouTube Shorts, use the 9:16 vertical preset instead.
tools.aspect-ratio-calculator.faqs.4.que: What is the difference between 16:9 and 4:3?
tools.aspect-ratio-calculator.faqs.4.ans: 16:9 is a widescreen format that is wider relative to its height, standard for modern displays and video. 4:3 is the older, more square-shaped format used by classic TVs and some presentation slides.
tools.aspect-ratio-calculator.faqs.5.que: How do I find the width if I know the height and aspect ratio?
tools.aspect-ratio-calculator.faqs.5.ans: Select a preset ratio or enter your known dimensions to lock the ratio. Then change the height field to your target value and the width will be calculated automatically.
tools.aspect-ratio-calculator.guide.intr: What Is the Aspect Ratio Calculator?

The Aspect Ratio Calculator helps you determine the proportional relationship between width and height for any dimensions. Enter a width and height to instantly see the simplified ratio, or lock a ratio and let the tool auto-calculate the missing dimension when you change one value.

This is essential for designers, video editors, photographers, and developers who need to resize content while maintaining correct proportions. The visual preview shows you exactly how the dimensions look relative to each other.
tools.aspect-ratio-calculator.guide.sect: How to Use the Aspect Ratio Calculator
Enter your width and height values in pixels. The simplified aspect ratio appears instantly below the inputs.
Click the lock button between the width and height fields to lock the current ratio. When locked, changing one dimension automatically updates the other to maintain the proportion.
Use the preset buttons (16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 21:9, 9:16, 3:2) to quickly apply common aspect ratios. The calculator keeps your current width and adjusts the height to match.
The visual preview on the right updates in real time to show you the shape of your dimensions.
Unlock the ratio at any time to freely edit both dimensions independently.

16:9 is the standard widescreen ratio used by most monitors, TVs, and YouTube videos. 4:3 is the classic TV and presentation format. 1:1 is a perfect square, commonly used for social media profile images and Instagram posts. 21:9 is the ultrawide cinema format. 9:16 is vertical video for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts. 3:2 is the traditional photography ratio used by most DSLR cameras.
Calculating video export dimensions for specific platforms
Resizing images for web design while preserving proportions
Determining the correct resolution for monitor or display setups
Planning responsive layouts that maintain visual consistency
Converting between standard aspect ratios for print and digital media

The tool finds the greatest common divisor (GCD) of your width and height, then divides both values by it. For example, 1920 and 1080 share a GCD of 120, giving you 16:9. When the ratio is locked, the tool stores the decimal ratio and uses it to calculate the complementary dimension as you type.

tools.aba-routing-number-validator.guide: What is an ABA routing number?

An ABA routing number — also called a routing transit number (RTN) — is the nine-digit code that identifies a US bank or credit union in ACH transfers, Fedwire payments and direct deposits. It is assigned by the American Bankers Association and tells the payment network exactly which institution to route the money to.

You can find your routing number on the bottom-left of a paper check (the first group of nine digits), in your bank's mobile app, or on its website. Large banks often use several routing numbers depending on the state where you opened the account and the type of payment.
How to validate a routing number
Type or paste the 9-digit routing number into the field above.
The tool instantly runs the 3-7-1 weighted checksum (mod 10) that every valid routing number must satisfy.
The first two digits are decoded to show the Federal Reserve district and the institution type behind the number.
A green result means the checksum is valid and the prefix is recognized; a red result means the number cannot exist.
Use the verified number in ACH, wire and direct-deposit forms as usual.
Routing numbers are public information — checking one is completely safe.
Large banks can have dozens of routing numbers, split by state or account type, so make sure the number belongs to the state of your account.
Some banks use different routing numbers for wire transfers than for ACH and direct deposit — check which one the form asks for.
What is an ABA routing number?

It is the nine-digit code that identifies a US bank or credit union when money moves through ACH, Fedwire or a direct deposit. It was introduced by the American Bankers Association in 1910 and is printed on every US check.

The first, fourth and seventh digits are multiplied by 3, the second, fifth and eighth by 7, and the third and sixth by 1. Adding these products and taking the result modulo 10 must give 0 — the last digit of the routing number makes that true. This catches nearly every typo.
Where do I find my routing number?

Look at the bottom-left corner of a paper check — the nine-digit group between the symbols is the routing number. You can also find it in your banking app, on your bank's website, or on your account statements.
Can two banks share the same routing number?

No. Every routing number points to exactly one institution. However, one bank can hold many routing numbers — large banks assign different numbers per state, and often separate ones for wires, ACH and paper checks.

tools.swift-bic-checker.guide.whatIs.bod: A SWIFT code — formally a BIC, defined by ISO 9362 — is the international identifier a bank needs to receive cross-border wires. It is 8 or 11 characters long: four letters identifying the bank, two letters for the country, two alphanumeric characters for the city, and an optional three-character branch code.

When you send an international transfer, the SWIFT network uses this code to reach the right bank in the right country. Codes ending in XXX (or with no branch part at all) refer to the bank's primary office. SWIFT and BIC are two names for exactly the same thing.
tools.swift-bic-checker.guide.howTo.titl: How to check a SWIFT/BIC code
tools.swift-bic-checker.guide.howTo.item: Type or paste the 8- or 11-character code into the field above.
The tool checks the structure and verifies that positions 5-6 are a real ISO country code.
Each segment is displayed with its meaning: bank code, country, location and branch.
The character in position 8 flags test and training BICs that never carry real payments.
If the code is in the bundled database of 51,000+ banks, you will see the bank's name, city and country.
tools.swift-bic-checker.guide.tips.title: Tips
tools.swift-bic-checker.guide.tips.items: DEUTDEFF and DEUTDEFFXXX are the same thing — both point to the primary office.
Banks merge and codes change, so confirm the BIC with the recipient before wiring money.
A SWIFT code identifies the bank only — it never contains an account number.
tools.swift-bic-checker.faqs.0.question: Is a SWIFT code the same as a BIC?
tools.swift-bic-checker.faqs.0.answer: Yes. SWIFT code and BIC (Bank Identifier Code) are two names for the same identifier defined by ISO 9362. Banks usually say SWIFT code, while the standard and regulatory documents say BIC.
tools.swift-bic-checker.faqs.1.question: How do I find my bank's SWIFT code?
tools.swift-bic-checker.faqs.1.answer: Check your bank's website — most publish their BIC on the contact or international transfers page. It is also printed on account statements and usually shown in the banking app. You can also paste the code here to confirm which bank it belongs to.
tools.swift-bic-checker.faqs.2.question: What does XXX at the end mean?
tools.swift-bic-checker.faqs.2.answer: XXX is the branch code for the bank's primary office. An 8-character code without a branch part and the same code with XXX added are identical — both refer to the head office.
tools.swift-bic-checker.faqs.3.question: Is it safe to share a SWIFT code?
tools.swift-bic-checker.faqs.3.answer: Yes. A BIC is public routing information, like a postal address for a bank. It identifies the institution only and contains no account details, so sharing it carries no risk.
